- **self**: Code comment narration and over-explanation (5/2)

## Definitions

- [statement] The characteristic narration tell is a comment that restates the adjacent code, adding maintenance burden and burying the few comments that matter. (low confidence) — https://github.com/takahirox/my-ai-employee/issues/76 · keywords: Code comment narration and over-explanation
- [statement] Comment-based detection is a weak, proxy signal: the repository study calls its results proxy-based and warns detectors both under- and over-estimate LLM use, and other work reports commercial detectors are affected by comments and unreliable. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01867v1 · keywords: Code comment narration and over-explanation · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.04704

## Structure and components

- [statement] Agent guidance for avoiding the tell: do not add comments by default; add one only for non-obvious why (rationale, constraints, invariants, trade-offs, surprising external behavior); prefer better names, types and structure over narration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-04) — https://github.com/takahirox/my-ai-employee/issues/76 · keywords: Code comment narration and over-explanation

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] LLM comments are not uniformly poor: in a 415-comment Java evaluation, human experts judged 58.8% to match originals and 27.7% to surpass them; automated metrics such as BLEU correlated negatively with human judgment. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2408.14007v3 · keywords: Code comment narration and over-explanation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A 2021-2025 study of eight GitHub repositories found comments flagged as likely LLM-generated concentrated in Meta and Explanation categories, and remained relatively stable over time. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-01) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.01867v1 · keywords: Code comment narration and over-explanation · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.04704
